title: A.C. Associates v. Metropolitan Steel Industries Inc.
citation: 1989 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 15053 (S.D.N.Y. 1989), as cited in the assignment
lead: An unpaid steel claimant tries to make a hospital’s acceptance of assigned contract rights carry the original contractor’s payment obligations.

actors.name: Presbyterian Hospital
actors.role: Hospital that engaged Walsh and later accepted an assignment.

actors.name: Walsh
actors.role: Construction contractor whose default led to termination of the main agreement.

actors.name: The steel claimant
actors.role: Unpaid participant in the subcontracting chain; its precise tier is qualified in the assigned account.

proceedings: The steel claimant sought payment from the hospital after Walsh’s default and termination.
The textbook reports dismissal of the complaint; complete judicial reasoning and the precise procedural scope remain unavailable.
limits: The cited opinion has not been recovered. The assignment’s simplified party relationships are qualified; its UCC and Restatement comparisons are editorial, not verified holdings of this construction case.

review.basis: Individually written and compared with the canonical full brief; no new independent opinion audit claimed.

sections.title: Walsh’s default leaves steel work unpaid
sections.cue: How did the hospital and the claimant become connected?
paragraphs: Presbyterian Hospital engaged Walsh for construction. Walsh engaged another firm for structural steel and other work. When Walsh defaulted, the hospital terminated the main construction agreement. A steel claimant alleged it had performed work before termination without receiving payment.

The assigned account calls the claimant a subcontractor while acknowledging it apparently was a sub-subcontractor; it says the court used simplified facts. That qualification matters because the available material does not independently establish every relationship in the contracting chain.

sources.pinpoint: Assigned printed 1218; contract chain and unpaid-work allegation

sections.title: The claimant relies on an assignment to seek payment from the hospital
sections.cue: What additional undertaking did its theory require?
paragraphs: The claimant relied on a document assigning Walsh’s contract with Metropolitan Steel to the hospital. It argued that the hospital’s acceptance made the hospital responsible for Walsh’s existing payment duty.

Receiving contract rights and undertaking someone else’s debts are distinct steps. The claimant needed the assignment and its acceptance to establish the latter. The full instrument and the parties’ complete arguments are not reproduced in the assignment.

sources.pinpoint: Assigned 1218; assignment and asserted payment duty

sections.title: The reported dismissal leaves its complete basis unavailable
sections.cue: Which textbook comparisons must remain separate from the result?
paragraphs: The textbook reports dismissal of the complaint but does not supply the entire judicial explanation, precise scope of dismissal or any opportunity to amend. Those features cannot be added to the reported outcome.

The editors then compare assignment and delegation under UCC § 2-210 and Restatement § 328. They expressly state that the UCC provision did not govern this case. Their sales-law analogy does not show that the district court applied Article 2 to this construction dispute, and the following land-sale and insecurity problems add no further holding here.

sources.pinpoint: Assigned 1218–1219; reported dismissal and editorial discussion
